1#main: The measure obligating challah, species that combine, and the law of exempt bread that became mixed with obligated. In it are 14 seifim. One is obligated in challah only from five species of grain; and one is obligated only with five quarters of a measure that holds forty-three and one-fifth eggs and a fifth of an egg; and one fills it with flour, and that flour is the measure of challah. And when one fills the measure with flour, it should be leveled and not heaped; and how they estimate to know it holds forty-three and one-fifth eggs was explained in Tur Orach Chaim (and see in Orach Chaim siman 456). And the weight of five quarters of flour is 520 Egyptian drachma of wheat flour from Egypt. {Rama: A vessel holding ten fingerbreadths by ten fingerbreadths in height of three fingerbreadths and a ninth of a finger approximately is the measure of challah; and likewise a measure that has seven fingerbreadths less two ninths of a finger [by seven less two ninths of a finger] in height seven fingerbreadths less two ninths of a finger is the omer; and all these fingerbreadths are the width of the thumb of the hand (Rambam, chapter 6 of Bikkurim).}
2#main: The five species of grain combine—if the dough has only five quarters from all five of them, they combine. In what case is this said? When they were mixed as flour; but if each was kneaded alone and does not have the measure, and he attached it to another species, they do not combine except in this order: wheat combines only with spelt; spelt combines with each one; barley combines with all except wheat; oats combine with barley and spelt and not with oats and wheat; oats combine with barley and spelt and not with wheat and oats. And for the Rambam, spelt, oats, and oats combine. And if each species was kneaded alone and has the measure and he wishes to separate from this species upon that—they separate only from its own species. How so? They do not separate wheat upon any of them, nor any of them upon wheat; spelt and oats separate from one upon the other, and likewise oats and barley separate from one upon the other. {Rama: If he mixed a kav of dough with another kav of dough not of its kind and afterward divided them and added to each a quarter-kav of its kind—it is obligated in challah, since they did not combine when mixed; but if he mixed a kav of flour with a kav of flour of another kind intending to divide them [and divided them] and added to each a quarter-kav of its kind—it is exempt (Tur).}
3#main: These five quarters—the leaven, bran, and coarse bran combine to complete the measure if he kneaded without sifting; but if he sifted and separated coarse bran from them and returned and mixed them with it, it does not combine.
4#main: A kav of wheat on this side and a kav of barley on this side and a kav of spelt in the middle joining them—behold these combine, and he must separate from each species and species.
5#main: Half a kav of wheat on this side and half a kav of barley on this side and half a kav of spelt in the middle—they combine, and he tithes from the spelt upon all three.
6#main: A kav of wheat on this side and a kav of wheat on this side and a kav of rice in the middle—or a kav of a gentile, or a kav of challah—they do not combine. (But if there was dough between them from which challah was already taken, they combine (Rosh, general rule 2).)
7#main: If between them was a kav of one of the five species, or a kav belonging to another woman—they combine.
8#main: A kav of new grain and a kav of old—they do not combine. If there was a kav of old on this side and a kav of old on this side and new in the middle—they combine. (And the same applies in reverse—new on two sides and old in the middle (Beit Yosef).)
9#main: One who makes dough from wheat and rice—if it has taste of grain, it is obligated in challah, even though most is rice; and if not, it is exempt.
10#main: If he placed leaven from wheat dough into rice dough—if it has taste of grain, it is obligated in challah.
11#main: If he placed leaven from dough from which challah was not taken into dough from which challah was taken, and all are one species—if he has flour or dough from which challah was not taken, he separates from it upon this leaven proportionally—meaning one forty-eighth in the leaven (and even if this has no measure of challah, provided he leaves it with the large dough (as implied in Terumat HaDeshen siman 100)). And if not, he separates one forty-eighth from all the dough, since all of it became tevel. And the same law if the leaven is exempt and the dough is obligated. {Rama: Nevertheless l'chatchila he should not rely on this and should not place exempt leaven in obligated dough (Mordechai, chapter Makom SheNahagu). But if he already transgressed and did so, it is permitted l'chatchila to take from that dough and place in another dough to be leaven (Terumat HaDeshen siman 100).}
12#main: One for whom bread from which he separated challah became mixed with bread from which he did not separate—if he has flour, he makes dough of five quarters and mixes it with the loaves in a vessel and separates from it for those loaves that became mixed. And if he wishes to separate from it itself, he must separate a little from each loaf and loaf; or he mixes them all in one vessel and separates from each one upon all until he separates according to the calculation of the loaves—and one more; such as if five from which challah was taken became mixed in ten from which challah was not taken, he separates from six, for then he certainly separated from one upon which challah was not taken. {Rama: A baker who spreads a pie from dough from which challah was not taken and meat is inside—it is permitted to separate from another dough obligated in challah upon this one, and the taste of the dough entering the meat is also released (Beit Yosef in the name of a responsum).}
13#main: Dough that does not have the measure, and at the time of baking it swelled and grew until it appears as if it has the measure—it is exempt. (And the same if it swelled before baking (Beit Yosef and responsum of the Rosh general rule 2 and Rashba siman 461).)
14#main: It is forbidden to make one's dough less than the measure in order to release from it the obligation of challah.
